correctness.rationale: For integers a<b the cube intersected with integral sum slab has only 0/1 vertices: two fractional coordinates permit opposite perturbations, one fractional coordinate and an active sum equality forces its value integral. Hence it equals the consecutive-layer hull. A Euclidean r-ball center c is feasible iff r<=ci<=1-r and a+r sqrt(d)<=sum ci<=b-r sqrt(d). Intersecting the two possible coordinate-sum intervals [dr,d(1-r)] and [a+r sqrt(d),b-r sqrt(d)] gives exactly the four stated bounds. An all-equal center reaches any feasible sum. At optimum, first three active bounds force a unique center; when only strict fourth slab barrier is active, the feasible incenter locus is a nondegenerate (d-1)-dimensional hyperplane cut. All d>=2 and integer 0<=a<b<=d handled symbolically; enumeration to d<=100 is corroboration.
